# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-Vfu` — app UI can't reach the spilled request detail

**Fixed** on this head (commit `3f4ef0ad03`).

The app Request tab now surfaces the same pointer the CLI `/trajectory inspect` renders:

- `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_details_tabs.dart` (`_requestPage`) gained a **"Request blob"** row (`strings.requestSpillFile`) rendered whenever `detail.spillFile != null`, grouped with the prompt/manifest hash pointer rows. A new fixture (`spilledAssistant` in `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/fixture_details.dart`) pins it: `packages/fa_ui/test/trajectory/trajectory_details_test.dart`, test *"gh-1745: a spilled request names its blob; the stub messages carry no dangling colon"*.
- The tab's inline per-message list skips the empty preview `Text` for stub messages (the text rides the blob) instead of rendering blank lines.
- The dangling-colon renderer is gone from both surfaces the thread named:
  - `_requestSummaryText` (copy-to-clipboard) — new `_requestStubLine` helper emits `role · N chars` with no `: ` tail when `preview.isEmpty`;
  - `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` Markdown export — same guard; spilled sessions export `- \`user\` 10 chars` (test: `test/trajectory/trajectory_export_test.dart`, *"gh-1745: a spilled request summary exports without dangling colons"*).

Resolution choice: we surface the `spillFile` row rather than resolving the blob content in-tab — the details tabs are pure widgets over the snapshot with no `ExecutionEnv` reach, and the pointer keeps parity with the CLI viewer. Scoping the PR to the CLI host is unnecessary now that the app side has its pointer.

The ticket (input/ticket.md, Problem Summary) cites two unrotated record kinds in the 1 GB session: `model_request_summary` at 658.75 MB **and `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB (2487 records)**. This PR remediates only `model_request_summary`; nothing here touches `shell_job_registry`, so a marathon session still grows unboundedly — just ~4× slower — while the issue auto-closes.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: TTL never advances for ended sessions — no boot-time/global sweep**

`enforceBudget()` is only ever called from `_maybeSweep()` inside [write] — i.e. rotation runs only while *that session* keeps receiving requests. Once a session ends, its `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` dir stops aging: 30-day-old blobs of dead sessions stay forever, and `.fah/trajectories/` accumulates up to 50 MB × N sessions with no reaper. The ticket's letter is per-session ("max 50MB per session"), so this isn't blocking — but the disk-footprint tail the ticket complains about partially survives at the directory level.

Cheap fix: on host boot (or session open), sweep every sibling `requests/` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` against the same TTL — `enforceBudget` already has the age math, it just needs a variant that takes the dir explicitly.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u-VlX` — TTL never advances for ended sessions

**Implemented** (commit `8ed87b6cfb`), exactly the cheap shape the thread proposed:

- `TrajectoryRequestBlobStore.sweepExpiredEverywhere()` — walks every `<session>/requests` dir under `.fah/trajectories/` and deletes every blob past `ttlDays`, applying the same age math as `enforceBudget` but **without the newest-kept grace**: a dead session keeps nothing past the TTL (with the grace rule its last blob would survive forever — the exact leak the thread points at).
- `sweepOncePerBoot()` runs it once per store instance. The store is built lazily at the session's first request, so the sweep fires at *session open* on both hosts (CLI `trajectory_commands.dart`, app `agent_service_lifecycle.dart`) with zero extra host wiring.
- Best-effort like the rest of rotation: a missing root or failed listing is a no-op, removal failures are swallowed.

Tests (`test/trajectory/trajectory_request_blobs_test.dart`, group *boot-time TTL sweep*): expired blobs across sibling session dirs are pruned (count returned), fresh blobs and the live session's own blob survive, a missing trajectories root is a no-op, and the first write sweeps stale siblings. CLI e2e (`test/cli/agent_cli_request_blobs_test.dart`): a 40-day-old blob of a dead session is gone after one real session runs.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1745 correctly moves the heavy `model_request_summary` payloads (per-message block texts, raw wire dumps) out of the session JSONL into a rotated `.fah/trajectories/<sid>/requests/` blob dir with a working kill switch, graceful inline fallback, and preserved usage-fold basis (Σ `chars` survives the stub). Verified: 156 cli/trajectory/config tests, 225 trajectory tests, 152 usage/CLI-e2e tests, and both new app tests pass; `dart analyze` clean.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ App host spills but its UI can't reach the blob — the Request tab renders empty previews and only the CLI `/trajectory inspect` names the spill file (comment 1)
- ⚠️ Ticket also cites `shell_job_registry` at 215.92 MB; PR says "Closes #1745" without touching it (comment 2)
- 💡 Ended sessions' blobs never age out (TTL advances only on writes); dead `requestBlobMaxBytes` getter; untested `_trajectoryYaml` save path; one unrelated reformat (comments 3–6)

**Next Steps**:
1. Surface the spill pointer (or blob content) in the app/fa_ui Request tab
2. Confirm a follow-up issue covers `shell_job_registry` growth before auto-closing gh-1745
3. Optional polish: boot-time TTL sweep, use `requestBlobMaxBytes`, save-path test, revert the formatting-only hunk
